This is widely documented as one of the biggest upsets in World Cup history, with Argentina coming in as a very strong favorite and Saudi Arabia ranked 51st in the FIFA rankings at the time [1].

The node’s probability should represent:

> The **pre‑match implied chance that Saudi Arabia would win the match in regulation** (i.e., excluding draws), as reflected by betting/market odds just before kickoff.

  - Argentina win: ~87%  
  - Remaining 13% is split between Saudi win and draw.
- Typical elite‑vs‑minnow World Cup group‑stage odds (for a team as strong as Argentina vs a team ranked ~50th) usually put:
  - Argentina win in the 75–85% range,
  - Draw around 10–18%,
  - Saudi win around 3–10%, depending on book and overround.

- Your starting anchor (market ~87% for Argentina) leaves only 13% total for draw + Saudi.
- In such a split, markets generally assign more weight to the draw than to the extreme underdog win.

A reasonable decomposition of that ~13% remainder would be roughly:

- Draw: ~8–10%
- Saudi win: ~3–5%

This aligns with how bookmakers usually price three‑way outcomes in highly uneven fixtures.

- USA being clearly stronger than at least one or two group opponents,
- Reasonable but not overwhelming risk from injuries and variance,

### Actionable takeaway
